_doc: Per-repo editor/agent dotfiles, built and deployed with the same src → build.sh → dist → target shape as 9_others. Adding a tool = one entry in `targets` plus a directory under src/dotfiles/. Nothing here is machine-specific: see `never_manage`.
_portability: This module is designed to be copied verbatim into any repo (unix, tools, front-data, ...). It has no dependency on cloud's TypeScript engines — build.sh's `dotfiles` verb is plain POSIX file copying, so a repo needs only 9_others/src/dotfiles/ + the verb.
_never_manage_doc: Per-machine state, NOT configuration. .obsidian/workspace*.json holds pane ids and layout for one device; .claude/settings.local.json is the documented place for local overrides. Deploy copies file-by-file and never purges the target directory, so these survive untouched — overwriting them would clobber another device's layout on every build.
_deploy_semantics: Additive per file. dist/dotfiles/<tool>/* is copied over <repo>/<target>/, creating the directory if needed. The target is NEVER emptied first (unlike 9_others' dist purge) precisely because these directories mix managed config with unmanaged machine state.
_sot_sources_doc: Where src/<tool>/ is REFRESHED FROM before deploy, so what every repo ships is generated rather than hand-kept. Same shape and same reason as the root_targets refresh from 1_cloud-configs/dist/: a copy nothing regenerates drifts, and drift is invisible here because each copy's own _doc claims to be the shared file. mcp-auth-headers.sh proved it — cloud-infra's three copies still said cloud-infra-mcp months after the rename to c3-infra-mcp, while the copy actually deployed into the repos said the new name. Cosmetic that time; the next one would not have been.
_sot_sources_resolution: Resolved against $CLAUDE_SOT_DIR first (the override the flakes already use), then <repo>/../cloud-u-linux/<path> for the sibling checkout layout. Both missing = no-op, and the committed src/ copy is used unchanged, so the module stays portable into repos with no my-ai checkout (see _portability).
_sot_sources_scope: BY NAME, and only names present in BOTH sides. settings.json is deliberately not refreshed: it is a subset mirror of the machine-independent half of settings.base.json, not a copy of any one SoT file, and nothing in the SoT is named settings.json — so name-matching excludes it by construction rather than by a special case someone has to remember to keep.
_root_targets_doc: Single files deployed to the repo ROOT rather than into a directory. .mcp.json is Claude Code's project-scoped MCP server registry. cloud used to carry it as a tracked symlink to /home/diego/.mcp.json, which resolved on exactly one laptop and dangled in every clone, CI runner and container — and Claude Code loads NO servers when .mcp.json cannot be read, silently. src/apps/root/mcp.json is a real file so each repo is self-contained. In cloud it is refreshed from 1_cloud-configs/dist/mcp.json, which derive-mcp-json.ts generates from the .mcp blocks in a_solutions/*/build.json. sops.yaml is per-REPO, not universal: cloud encrypts four patterns (secrets.yaml, secrets_backup.yaml, jwks_key.yaml, terraform.tfstate.enc) while unix encrypts its own set, and most repos have none at all. The mapping here is shared; the file each repo supplies under src/apps/root/ is its own. A repo with no src/apps/root/sops.yaml simply skips it. sops.yaml now lives in the 2_sops/ tier rather than under 0_apps/src/root/, since sops is its own concern; deploy-dotfiles.sh looks there for it.
